objective: Proof. (1) The twist criterion: for a knot's space H and a set t of incidences, H with the incidences in t twisted is non-colourable iff t is a cocycle (an edge cut) of the incidence graph (switching gives one direction; sign-nonsingularity and the uniqueness of Pfaffian signings up to switching give the other). (2) So the two sides of a nontrivial cut both accept knots only when the cut has two edges: complementary parity cosets force every even set of cut edges to be a cocycle, so the cut edges lie in series around a cycle of blobs and the shores alternate, which leaves both shores connected only for two edges. Checked: the criterion on every twist of every nontrivial 2- and 3-edge cut of ten knot's spaces and on random incidence sets; every nontrivial 4-edge cut of four small spaces; controls.
status: Proved by NATIVE-PATHS-20261101-001C-P001: a knot's space stays non-colourable under a twist pattern exactly when the pattern is a cocycle of its incidence graph (switching one way; sign-nonsingularity and the uniqueness of Pfaffian signings up to switching the other), so if both sides of a nontrivial cut accept knots on its channels the cut has exactly two edges: knot meets knot only pairwise; checked on all 1568 twists of the 2- and 3-edge cuts of ten spaces, 1200 random sets and cocycles, and the side relations of 450 cuts including 234 four-edge cuts
title: Knot meets knot only pairwise: failure is invariant exactly under cuts
